//: Mutation matrix for THE DISPLAY RULE (issue #202), driven by probe_displaytitle. Every mutant is labelled with the DIRECTION it breaks in, because a one-directional matrix proves nothing here. A rule that returns '' for everything passes every 'no credential on screen' assertion by showing nothing; a rule that returns its input passes every 'a real title survives' assertion by being a no-op AND is the bug being fixed. Half of these LEAK a credential; half EAT a legitimate title. Nothing in this file is a real credential - every token, salt and password in the probe is invented.

mutants.name: LEAKS-url-candidate-accepted-as-a-title
mutants.//: Direction: LEAK. Drop the scheme test in isUsable and mpv's media-title - which for a stream carrying no metadata IS the signed url - becomes an acceptable label again. This is issue #202 itself, restored in one line.

mutants.name: LEAKS-query-tail-slice-accepted-as-a-title
mutants.//: Direction: LEAK. The #200 shape - '<id>?t=<token>&s=<salt>', a completeBaseName() slice sitting in a title field written by an older build. It carries no scheme, so only the query-tail test catches it.

mutants.name: LEAKS-derivation-is-completeBaseName-again
mutants.//: Direction: LEAK, and it is the original bug verbatim: the idiom that produced #193 increment 5, #200 and #202. Put back here it makes the last-resort label a slice of the signed url's QUERY.

mutants.name: LEAKS-derivation-returns-the-location-verbatim
mutants.//: Direction: LEAK-adjacent. Scrubbed of its query, so no invented secret survives - and it puts 'https://music.example.com/rest/stream.view' on screen as the name of a song, which is the shape the issue calls a log-safe string that is not a good label. Section 6's '://' assertion is what refuses it.

mutants.name: LEAKS-first-candidate-scrubbed-instead-of-skipped
mutants.//: Direction: LEAK-adjacent, and the distinction this whole header exists to make. Cleaning a url candidate instead of rejecting it yields 'https://music.example.com/rest/stream.view' - no credential, a terrible name for a song, and it silently outranks the perfectly good queue title sitting in the next argument.

mutants.name: EATS-every-title-containing-a-question-mark
mutants.//: Direction: OVER-EAGER, and the failure mode the issue warns about by name. 'Who Framed Roger Rabbit?' is a title. A sanitiser that eats it is a worse bug than the leak, because it is silent and it fires every day rather than on one screenshot.

mutants.name: EATS-everything-nothing-is-ever-usable
mutants.//: Direction: DO-NOTHING BIAS. Reject every candidate and the rule passes every single NOLEAK assertion in the probe by never showing a real title at all. This is the mutant that proves those assertions are not the whole test.

mutants.name: EATS-the-derivation-entirely
mutants.//: Direction: DO-NOTHING BIAS, the other half, and it covers the local-file case too. Deriving nothing is trivially leak-free; it also blanks the now-playing overlay for every stream that carries no metadata - which is every Subsonic stream, i.e. the exact case this issue is about - and takes a local file's base name away with it.

mutants.name: EATS-second-candidate-never-consulted
mutants.//: Direction: DO-NOTHING BIAS. Skipping the second candidate is invisible to every url assertion and destroys the actual fix: the mpv site's whole point is that when mpv hands back a url, the HOST's queue title takes over. Without this line the overlay falls all the way through to the location.
